video_title: Deron Williams on Chris Paul Rivalry, NBA Politics & Why He Retired Early

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the difficulty of transitioning after retiring from basketball
quotes.excerpt: life after basketball is crazy. It's a lot of ups and downs. It's definitely a journey.
quotes.quote: Life after basketball is crazy. It's a lot of ups and downs. It's definitely a journey when you leave. They try to prepare you, but there's no way to prepare you. We've been playing basketball literally our whole life, and then now it's like, okay, basketball is up, do something else now.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his background in wrestling and combat sports
quotes.excerpt: my first sport growing up was wrestling. I wrestled for nine years, was state champ twice.
quotes.quote: My first sport growing up was wrestling. I wrestled for nine years, was state champ twice in Texas. So I always loved combat sports, and always loved the UFC and MMA. I've been training for years and I'm actually part owner of a gym in Dallas called Fortis MMA. I got a call that Frank Gore was looking for a boxing opponent. I had never boxed, but I did a lot of striking and stand-up, so I felt pretty confident. Nate Robinson didn't really research either, because I think he thought Jake Paul was just a YouTuber and he didn't really, like Jake grew up wrestling, like he's tough. And he had already been fighting. And Nate thought he was just going to come out there off athleticism and it ain't like that, man.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on training for his boxing match
quotes.excerpt: I just did all my training at my MMA gym. My business partner is the head coach.
quotes.quote: I just did all my training at my MMA gym. My business partner is the head coach, Sayif Saud, and he's coached UFC title fights. We have 20-plus athletes in the UFC, so he knows what it takes on the highest level. I wasn't going up against a world champion boxer, I'm fighting another athlete, so I felt pretty confident.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his basketball influences growing up
quotes.excerpt: I watched Magic, Stockton, Gary Payton, Jason Kidd, Jason Kidd, Allen Iverson, Baron Davis, Steve Francis.
quotes.quote: My mom played in college, small college in West Virginia, and that's where she met my dad. They both played basketball in college. I had a bunch of cousins that played college basketball that were older than me, so I always loved basketball. Basketball was always my first love. As far as players I watched, of course Magic, Stockton, Gary Payton, Jason Kidd, Jason Kidd, Allen Iverson, Baron Davis, Steve Francis, and all, I mean, AI, Staff, Baron Davis, Steve Francis, people don't talk about Baron Davis or Steve Francis, like they don't get enough respect, it seems like, because those were some cold point guards.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the point guards he studied
quotes.excerpt: I think Jason Kidd, his passing ability, looking at him being a bigger point guard.
quotes.quote: I think Jason Kidd, his passing ability, looking at him being a bigger point guard, seeing how he controlled the game. I took, of course watched AI and Steve Francis, their crossovers and kind of, obviously you couldn't really do AI's crossover by the time I got to the league, but Steve Francis had this crossover where he would kind of just like throw it over. So I mean, I tried to study the game, watch guys, and you know, take little things here and there.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on when he realized the NBA was realistic
quotes.excerpt: not till college, not till like probably after my sophomore year, going into my last year.
quotes.quote: Not till college, not till like probably after my sophomore year, going into my last year of college, honestly. And maybe, maybe not even really till we went on that run with Illinois. Like I wasn't, I wasn't McDonald's, I wasn't, even coming into Illinois, it was Dee Brown, like Dee Brown was the man. We were same class, but he was McDonald's All-American point guard. I wasn't. So I kind of always flew under the radar my whole career, my whole life. You know, even like high school was Bracey Wright, you remember Bracey Wright? So he was McDonald's, he was my teammate.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his difficult rookie season with Jerry Sloan
quotes.excerpt: I had a rough rookie season because I played for Jerry Sloan who didn't really like rookies.
quotes.quote: I had a rough rookie season because I played for Jerry Sloan who didn't really like rookies. He didn't like rookies, he wanted to make you work for it. It's almost like test you, you know, test your resolve, test how you're going to respond, which it took me, it took me some time to, you know, really see that. And even I don't think I really saw it in the moment, right? I just, I just thought he was being an asshole, right? And so once I left and looked back and, you know, you get older, you mature, you see, you see things a lot differently, right? And you see why, okay, this is why he did it.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his rookie year teammates
quotes.excerpt: I wasn't, I wasn't McDonald's, I wasn't, even coming into Illinois, it was Milt Palacio and Keith McLeod.
quotes.quote: I wasn't, I wasn't McDonald's, I wasn't, even coming into Illinois, it was Milt Palacio and Keith McLeod. And a lot of people be like, who are they? Right? And there's no knock on them because they helped me so much. Like I learned a lot from those guys, my rookie year, right? They took me under their wing, showed me, showed me the ropes, but I think most of the people on the team know who, who the best point guard was. And we, we ended up, we ended up going 41 and 41 my rookie year. Could have made the playoffs, missed the playoffs by one game. I feel like if I was, kind of starting from the beginning of the season and getting 30, you know, minutes a game like CP and some of these other guys was, we would have, we would have been better.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan's strict team rules
quotes.excerpt: he was super old school, right? Like we, we'd be on the bus and we couldn't use our phones.
quotes.quote: He was super old school, right? Like we, we'd be on the bus and we couldn't talk on, we couldn't use our phones on the bus. So like we get on the bus after a game, you want to call and talk to your, I got kids. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I want to call and talk to my kids. I have to get off the bus just to talk to my kids. Or like, say, say a teammate's running late. It's over with. I got to get off the bus to call him to be like, hey, where you at? So it was no, no phones on the bus. He just had a lot of like old school rules. Like I, huh? Was it micromanagement? No, I don't think it was. I think like I said, I think it was just he ran a tight ship. Like he, he, he, he, he, he tried to control things, but I think so it was very professional. He wanted to be professional, right? It's like, you can listen to music in your headphones, but don't have a speaker blaring. Have a speaker blaring. Like, and he would tell you like, I think the stuff on the bus was like, he's like, you know, take your headphones off, get to know one of your teammate, like talk to your teammates.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on Karl Malone joining the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: when Karl Malone went to LA, he went to the Lakers for that last season.
quotes.quote: You hear a story about, I think when Karl Malone went to LA, he went to the Lakers for that last season. And somebody, they, I guess all the guys had on their headphones, and he came on the bus and was taking, knocking guys' headphones off like, get to know, you know, get to know your teammate. So, I think it was just little things he did. I don't, I think it was controlled, but it wasn't like, again, looking back, controlling in a bad way. It was just like, he wanted to be professional.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the culture of the Utah Jazz
quotes.excerpt: we practiced hard as fuck. We was always in shape. We drilled the fuck out of our offense.
quotes.quote: We practiced hard as fuck. We was always in shape. We drilled the fuck out of our offense. We, you know, had to play defense. So, yeah, I mean, from that standpoint, like it, we, like we practiced the same way we did in training camp all the way, all the way up to like January, February. We're still running suicides at the end of practice and shit. Like, but other than when I got to other teams, we wasn't doing that. We were barely practicing, yeah, we were barely practicing, barely playing five-on-five.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his trade from the Utah Jazz to the Nets
quotes.excerpt: the Magic told me if I signed my ETO, whatever that was called back then, they were going to send me.
quotes.quote: The Magic told me if I signed my ETO, whatever that was called back then, they were going to send me straight to Brooklyn. I was like, man, I'm going to Brooklyn. I was just telling him about it. And they sent me to the Lakers where I didn't want to go. I was pissed. I was pissed. I did not want to go to the Lakers. I was like, I want to go to Brooklyn.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the Carmelo Anthony trade situation
quotes.excerpt: that was the year Carmelo was like, he was either going to Brooklyn or New York.
quotes.quote: That was the year Carmelo was like, he was either going to Brooklyn or New York. And so basically, Denver was like negotiating with both of those teams, right? And then Carmelo, I think ultimately had the decision or I don't know, I don't know how it worked, but he, as soon as he got traded to New York, I think the GM from Utah, Kevin O'Connor was monitoring it and basically was like, I'm not putting them two together. No, he just said, he offered like the same offer that Brooklyn had offered. They basically took that for me.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan's resignation
quotes.excerpt: Coach Sloan quit because we got into it at halftime. And I've told the story.
quotes.quote: Coach Sloan quit because we got into it at halftime. And I've told the story. I called a play to one side of the floor, it was usually on the other side of the floor, and he didn't like that. I just kind of made it on the fly. And he quit. And when so then he we came in at halftime and he's like, you want to coach this team? And I'm like, I don't want to coach and then he basically was like, told the owner, he's like, can I talk to you? And I was like, no, let me come into, let me be a part of this conversation. And basically he said he was quitting, and I was like, no, don't do that, just trade me.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the injuries that impacted his career
quotes.excerpt: on paper we were supposed to be really good. And we had a lot of injuries.
quotes.quote: On paper we were supposed to be really good. And we had a lot of injuries. So Brook got hurt that year. He had kept messing his foot up. Had a pretty, pretty bad foot. So I think he missed the whole, I don't know, I can't remember. He missed most of the season. I came into the season hurt. I had an ankle injury that nagged me for the whole season. Paul got hurt for a stretch of the season. KG was out there on one leg the whole season. And you can't get KG to sit the fuck down. Like, we like, ticket, go sit, like we don't need you to practice, go sit down, but he can't, he can't stop. He can't. You think that's like, it's a act or like, if you don't know KG, right? Like look on, you like, is he really like this always on? And it's like, no, that's, that's him, like always want to compete, no matter what it is, practice, whatever. It's like, go, KG go sit down, please. He out there limping, limping around like, he wouldn't sit down. But, um, so we started out that season, we were trash. Like the record was trash because we had so many guys out and not playing and, um, we had a lot of expectations, but then we ended up, you know, making the playoffs, making a run the second half of the season, kind of getting guys in, um, you know, healthy and beat Toronto in the first round of the playoffs and then lost to Miami.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his trade to the Nets
quotes.excerpt: I was a Nets fan. So, you was my favorite player, and when you got traded to the Nets.
quotes.quote: I was a Nets fan. So, you was my favorite player, and when you got traded to the Nets, I'm like, shit, I finally got a, because we wasn't winning. So it was 24 wins. The year before that, it was fucking, I think 18 wins, you went before you was there. Yeah. I wasn't there for all 24 because I got traded after, uh, after the deadline. But, bro, it was, it was rough, man, because, um, I only lost, what, eight games in high school and 15 in college. Damn. And then I lost 41 my rookie, my rookie year. And then, and then I, I lost 41 my rookie, my rookie year.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on why he retired early
quotes.excerpt: I still love the game, but it's like, do I want to make this commitment of having to train.
quotes.quote: I still love the game, but it's like, do I want to make this commitment of having to train all the time? Like that sacrifice, like did, did your family life as far as like wanting to spend more time with your kids and stuff like that, was that one of the big reasons why you said, let me just, you know, because the kids are getting older, they're going to be off college soon. So let me, I mean, I had my, I had my fourth kid at 26. So, yeah, by, by the time, um, you know, I was 32, I think my daughter was, I think she was a freshman in high school, sophomore in high school, my oldest when I, when I kind of called it quits.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the physical toll of his career
quotes.excerpt: I had my fourth kid at 26. So, yeah, by, by the time, um, you know, I was 32.
quotes.quote: I had my fourth kid at 26. So, yeah, by, by the time, um, you know, I was 32, I think my daughter was, I think she was a freshman in high school, sophomore in high school, my oldest when I, when I kind of called it quits. Um, and so yeah, that was, that was a part of it, just being home, like I, I, like I think I took a little bit of time off, I, I think I had planned to come back or like see what happened. Um, but then I got home and I was just like, man, it's nice being home, not having to like, yeah, yeah, yeah, traveling, like the travel, NBA travel fucking sucks. It takes, it takes a lot out of you. Yeah, so I was just like, I'm done. I'm done.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on his mental state during his final years
quotes.excerpt: there was two things that, that I remember was Andrew Luck retired and he just kind of.
quotes.quote: There was two things that, that I remember was Andrew Luck retired and he just kind of, like, I can't remember what he said, but it resonated with me a lot. And then, remember when D Rose was going through his shit where he kind of wanted to like, just, did he, did he like leave the team or he just like kind of, you know what I'm talking about? Was it D Rose? I thought a couple players that, that left out in the middle of the season. It wasn't for like a long time, but it was just like kind of he needed like some time, some time. And then, next day he resigned and then the story got out and then it was my fault. And then, um, yeah. And then that, that still stuck with me because I think, um, some shit happened in, um, I don't know if it was Brooklyn, it was, yeah, we were in Brooklyn with, with Avery, with Avery, yeah.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the 2000s Utah Jazz roster depth
quotes.excerpt: The eighth, ninth, tenth guys were MVPs of the league.

text_blocks.speaker: Deron Williams

The eighth, ninth, tenth guys were MVPs of the league.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on the evolution of point guards
quotes.excerpt: It's just combo guard. That's what you look like. Look at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.
quotes.quote: It's just different, man. Everything evolves. We were different point guards than the guys before us. It's the same thing with music. Pop has changed from the 80s to the 90s to the 2000s. It's just your preference. I think it's gone from being a traditional point guard to just combo guard. That's what you look like. Look at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. He's not a traditional point guard. Can he play point guard? Hell yeah. Especially in today's league. He still gets people involved. He's winning, he's making his teammates better. So is he a point guard? Yeah, to me he is. He's just not a traditional point guard. He's not going out there and trying to get 12 assists first.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's scoring and playmaking
quotes.excerpt: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is probably the closest to a combo guard.
quotes.quote: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is probably the closest to a combo guard. But Tyrese Haliburton averages 28, 29 a game. He's a combo guard. I don't think there's no real traditional point guard left. Tyrese Haliburton is the only one. And he can get dimes. He can get dimes. Tyrese Haliburton can get dimes. He's a scorer. He's a scorer. I didn't realize how cold Tyrese Haliburton was at really getting dimes until I seen he averages 11, 12 assists. That's so good. Multiple seasons though, he's led the league.

quotes.speaker: Dwight Howard
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard on the Washington Wizards' lack of success
quotes.excerpt: No matter how much talent they had, they never like, the arena just doesn't do it.
quotes.quote: But it's just Washington. Washington never good. It's like, no matter how much talent they had, they never like, the arena just doesn't do it. The arena doesn't do it. They don't get high like, there's no like real support. I don't know. But maybe it's because they were bad.

quotes.speaker: Dwight Howard
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard on Joel Embiid's need to manage minutes
quotes.excerpt: If Joel Embiid was to sacrifice his minutes so he can be healthy in the playoffs, they'll win.
quotes.quote: I believe if Joel Embiid was to sacrifice his minutes so he can be healthy in the playoffs, they'll win. He needs to come in and I saw he looked like he was in shape. He needs to get that. He needs that. At least for, you can't be too, you can't be the whole season. He can't be that big the whole season. I don't think he can sustain that weight for the rest of his career.

quotes.speaker: Dwight Howard
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard on the competitiveness of the NBA playoffs
quotes.excerpt: Last year in the playoffs, that's the most competition I seen throughout the whole playoffs.
quotes.quote: I think that this is going to be one of the hardest years to win a championship because everybody, like last year in the playoffs, that's the most competition I seen throughout the whole playoffs where everybody was going hard. Everybody. So I think this year is going to be like, because I don't know who's going to, like the West is up for grabs too. Yeah, I mean, San Antonio getting that experience should definitely help. They're going to have confidence. But it's all, it's luck, it's health, it's like, you know what I mean? So I don't, I don't know. There's a lot of good teams out there. Like we can't act like Paul George is not going to be, Jayson Tatum and they got a squad. They got a squad.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on wanting to play for the Denver Nuggets
quotes.excerpt: I would like to play in Denver with Nikola Jokic.
quotes.quote: I would like to play in Denver with Nikola Jokic. That would be tough. Because I'm good off the ball. I play well off the ball. So having a big that I can pick and roll, pick and pop with, and then he knows how to pass like that, like he's the point guard. I would like to play in Denver more than more than Victor Wembanyama, to be honest. But Victor Wembanyama on defense is a motherfucker. So having that, you know, behind you the whole game, whoa.

quotes.speaker: Deron Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Deron Williams on Victor Wembanyama's potential
quotes.excerpt: He's going to get six, seven, eight defensive player of the years.
quotes.quote: He's going to get six, seven, eight defensive player of the years. How, who's, how, how is he not? The man blocking three-point shots like they just like they normal shots. He is. And he's only getting stronger and better. So he might get, he might get that. He's going to get that.

quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard on his defensive legacy

I don't think you ever blocked my shot. Your floater? No.
